title: Applying a Task-Based Approach to Distributed Machine Learning Workflows
problem: Distributed ML training requires unified programming models for coordinating computational workloads across heterogeneous computing resources. ML model training for ECG-based medical classification needs efficient execution spanning from wearable edge data sources through distributed training infrastructure.
motivation: Distributed ML approaches enable real-time personalized healthcare through atrial fibrillation detection from wearable ECG devices, improving stroke care outcomes by monitoring modifiable risk factors.
method: The system uses a task-based programming model—breaking the training workflow into discrete, independently schedulable tasks—to coordinate machine learning training across distributed resources spanning wearable edge devices and central servers. One unified programming interface manages these tasks, specifying where and when each computation runs and orchestrating neural network training on heart rhythm data from PhysioNet. Trained models are then deployable directly onto wearables for real-time atrial fibrillation classification.
key_novelty: A single task-based programming model coordinates machine learning training across the entire path from wearable edge devices collecting data, through central servers, and back to wearable deployment.
contributions: Task-based programming approach for coordinating distributed ML workflows
Implementation of distributed ECG-based atrial fibrillation classification
Demonstration using PhysioNet database with edge device deployment
Unified model for composing components across edge-cloud computing continuum
limitations: The paper does not discuss computational requirements, comparison with existing distributed ML frameworks, scalability limitations, or performance metrics on the PhysioNet evaluation.
primary_theme: Distributed ML for healthcare edge computing
